summary: Suspected SAML assertion replay after clicking external vendor link; cross-account SSO sessions created
description:
Issue summary:
A Security Operations engineer flagged two unexpected SSO sessions created for a small set of developer accounts after those users clicked an external vendor link embedded in a voicemail transcription. The sessions were created via SAML assertions originating from our IdP (Okta). Initial hypothesis is an assertion replay or token-propagation from a vendor-hosted redirector.

Impact:
- 7 developer accounts observed with new SSO sessions within a 30-minute window on 2026-03-12 09:10-09:40 UTC.
- No privileged console changes observed; however several service tokens associated with developer CI were used shortly after the sessions.
- Potential lateral movement risk if assertion reuse allowed creation of service sessions.

Timeline (consolidated):
- 2026-03-12 09:02 UTC: Customer+Sales engineer receives voicemail with link; forwards to internal list.
- 2026-03-12 09:10 UTC: Users A, B, C click the link; Okta logs show AuthnRequest and Assertion issuance to SP app-client-id: sp-xy123.
- 2026-03-12 09:25 UTC: Alert from monitoring: spike in new SSO sessions (ids starting sso_9f*).
- 2026-03-12 09:33 UTC: Support receives inbound Slack from oncall reporting odd new sessions.
- 2026-03-12 10:00 UTC: Initial containment: force sign-out all web sessions for affected users; rotated associated API tokens for 2 CI service accounts.

Steps to reproduce / evidence to collect:
- Export Okta SAML assertion issuance logs for sp-xy123 between 2026-03-12 08:50 and 09:50 UTC.
- Retrieve web server access logs for callback endpoints used by the SP to identify source IPs and user-agents.
- Pull proxy logs for external link and redirect chain (we suspect vendor redirector hosted on vendor-cdn.example).
- List tokens used in the hour following sessions using token-usage audit logs; map to service accounts.

Initial findings / investigation notes:
- Assertion "SubjectConfirmation" recipient matched our SP endpoint and assertions were signed and had valid NotBefore/NotOnOrAfter windows. No immediate signature tampering detected.
- Several assertion issuance events include RelayState values pointing to a short-lived redirector URL hosted on vendor-cdn.example which returned a 302 to our SP endpoint.
- Source IPs for the redirector are geo-diverse (us-east and eu-west) and map to a third-party CDN provider.
- A small subset of the created SSO sessions had elevated session_duration limits (remember_me flag present). This matches a known vendor flow that sets an extended session cookie when returning from their auth proxy.
- Two CI service tokens (svc-ci-frontend, svc-ci-bench) showed new use 4-12 minutes after user sessions; investigation of those calls shows they originated from internal IP space but on hosts tied to the developer machines of affected users.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Forced logout for the 7 affected accounts across all sessions (Done 2026-03-12 10:00 UTC).
- Rotated API tokens for two service accounts most closely temporally correlated (Done 2026-03-12 10:15 UTC).
- Blocked vendor-cdn.example at corporate HTTP proxy pending vendor validation (Done 2026-03-12 11:00 UTC).
- Created temporary WAF rule to block requests with suspicious RelayState prefix used in the assertions (Done 2026-03-12 11:20 UTC).

Open hypotheses:
1) Vendor redirector captured a legitimate SAML assertion/use flow and replayed it to our SP for other recipients (assertion replay).
2) The vendor redirector performed a cross-origin framing or HTML injection that caused automatic POST of the assertion on behalf of clicking users.
3) User devices were already compromised and used the clicked flow to obtain valid assertions.

Next investigative actions:
- Confirm whether RelayState values are unique per session and whether they appear in vendor logs (request vendor for raw access logs, asked at 2026-03-12 12:05 UTC).
- Extract full SAML assertion samples (base64) for 3 events and perform canonicalization and signature verification chain trace. (Assigned to Marco DeLuca).
- Run forensic imaging on two developer workstations that correlated token use to ensure local compromise isn’t present (assigned to Desktop Forensics).
- Validate whether Okta session issuance triggered any downstream provisioning (SCIM events) during that window.

Resolution plan (short-term):
- Continue rotated tokens until root cause determined.
- If vendor confirms redirector was compromised, force a password reset and MFA re-enrollment for users who interacted with the vendor link (target: 2026-03-15).
- Implement assertion replay protection on SP: validate one-time RelayState nonce and short-lived assertion IDs against cache (engineering ticket created).

Follow-up / Post-incident items:
- Engineering ticket to add assertion nonce cache and replay protection (linked PRs in related_github_prs).
- Update phishing runbook with vendor-link handling guidance; create mandatory awareness note for Sales/Customer teams.
- Postmortem draft to be published to related_confluence_pages and shared with Risk and Legal for any compliance implications.
